why_now: The evidence suggests FormFactor moved from a flat year to a sharp upswing in about three quarters. FY25 revenue grew only 2.8% (USD 785.0M versus USD 763.6M), and Q3 FY25 revenue was down 2.5% year on year; then Q1 FY26 grew 32.0% and Q2 FY26 grew 31.9% (USD 258.2M), with record revenue, non-GAAP gross margin up from 38.5% (Q2 FY25) to 53.3% (Q2 FY26) and non-GAAP EPS from USD 0.27 to USD 0.82. Management and the 10-Q attribute the growth to HBM probe cards (about 75% of the Q2 year-on-year DRAM increase), foundry and logic probe cards for networking and HPC, and the Triton co-packaged-optics (CPO) test system. Other changes: a January 2026 restructuring to consolidate two California plants, the Keystone Photonics acquisition (December 2025, USD 20.6M), a new Texas factory due to start late Q4 FY26, and an 11 May 2026 Investor Day setting a 2030 target model of USD 1.6B revenue, 55% gross margin and USD 5.00 non-GAAP EPS. The quant screen ranks the stock 10th on 12-1 month momentum (+149%) and the stock is within 7% of its 52-week high, so much of the change is already in the price.
thesis: FormFactor makes wafer-test probe cards (about 81% of FY25 revenue) and probe stations, thermal and cryogenic systems used to test semiconductors before packaging. It is a second-order AI semiconductor-equipment beneficiary: more chiplets, taller HBM stacks and faster interfaces raise test intensity per wafer, which the company argues increases demand for its advanced MEMS probe cards and CPO test systems. Filing evidence shows a genuine inflection in revenue, gross margin and EPS, a nearly debt-free balance sheet (about USD 346M cash and securities, USD 11.6M debt) and a company-set 2030 target model. The research read is that FormFactor is a high-quality, AI-exposed cyclical with a real near-term upcycle, but at USD 149.15 (about USD 11.65B market cap, about 10.5x EV/annualised sales and about 43x annualised guided EPS) the market already capitalises that the 2030 target is achieved: USD 149 is about 30x the company's own 2030 EPS target of USD 5.00. For a several-fold outcome in 12-24 months, earnings would have to reach levels the company itself places five years out and the multiple would have to hold or expand. The evidence does not support that as a base case; the stock looks more like a strong business with an unfavourable risk/reward skew than an asymmetric 3-5x setup. Customer concentration (SK hynix about 24-27% of revenue) and memory-cycle exposure add drawdown risk if AI spending slows. Research read: interesting company, not an asymmetric 1-2 year opportunity at this price; keep on a watchlist for a price reset or evidence that revenue is tracking well ahead of the 2030 plan.
multibagger_mechanism: Testable chain for a 3x outcome (about USD 447), as model arithmetic: price = non-GAAP EPS x multiple. At 45x, EPS of about USD 9.9 is needed (about 2.9x the annualised Q3 FY26 guided USD 3.44 and about 2x the company's own 2030 target of USD 5.00); even on the company's 2030 target EPS of USD 5.00, USD 447 would be about 89x. Links: (a) HBM4/HBM4E test intensity and probe-card share gains persist (e3, e5); (b) CPO and GPU/ASIC probe cards ramp ahead of plan (e8, e9); (c) Farmers Branch lifts capacity and gross margin toward 55% sooner than 2030 (e7, e8); (d) the multiple stays at 40x+. Even a bull case where revenue reaches about USD 1.4B with 56% gross margin and 24% opex gives EPS near USD 4.6 and a price of USD 185-230 (1.25-1.55x) at 40-50x. The sourced evidence does not support a chain to 3x in 24 months; by my model estimate the probability of 3x or more is well under 5%.
expectations_gap: Reverse arithmetic: at USD 149.15 and 78.12M shares the equity value is about USD 11.65B and EV about USD 11.3B (cash and marketable securities USD 345.6M, debt USD 11.6M). That is about 12.5x trailing-four-quarter revenue (USD 902.2M) and about 10.5x the Q3 FY26 guided annualised revenue (USD 1,080M). On non-GAAP EPS it is about 68.7x the trailing four quarters (USD 2.17), about 43x annualised Q3 guided EPS of USD 0.86, and about 29.8x the company's 2030 target EPS of USD 5.00. In other words the price already capitalises the company's own five-year plan at a roughly 30x multiple, with the plan itself marked by the company as dependent on share gains in GPU, custom ASIC and CPO, markets it calls nascent with limited visibility. At 25x the 2030 target EPS the value would be about USD 125, below the current price even if the target is fully met. What the market may be right about: Q2 revenue and gross margin beat the top of guidance, the Q3 guide implies another record quarter, HBM4 test intensity is rising, and the company has hit its 2020 target model. What the market may be under-weighting: the Q3 guide midpoint is only +4.6% sequentially versus +14.2% in Q2; DRAM was +49% year on year in Q2 and could slow as HBM comparisons harden; SK hynix alone is 24-27% of revenue; revenue is not backed by a disclosed order backlog; and the gross margin jump included mix and utilisation benefits that may normalise. The Level-1 screen showed a low growth score (0.12) based on stale FY25 annual growth of +2.8%; the TTM picture is far stronger, so the screen understated the operating story but the valuation score (0.0) was fair. Sell-side consensus and price history could not be verified from an opened source in this session.

bull_case.name: bull
bull_case.description: Model-estimate scenario. HBM4/HBM4E, GPU/ASIC and CPO ramp ahead of the plan; revenue reaches about USD 1.4B annual run-rate within 24 months (versus the company's USD 1.6B 2030 target), non-GAAP gross margin about 56% as Farmers Branch ramps, opex about 24% of revenue, EPS about USD 4.6 on about 80M shares, and the market pays 40-50x. Implies roughly USD 185-230 per share. Probability 30%: needs the upcycle to run at or above the company's own multi-year trajectory without a memory pause and with the multiple holding.

base_case.name: base
base_case.description: Model-estimate scenario. Revenue grows toward about USD 1.15-1.25B with gross margin 52-54% and opex about 25-25.5% of revenue, non-GAAP EPS about USD 3.2-3.8, and the multiple compresses to 30-40x as growth slows toward the planned rate. Implies roughly USD 96-152 per share, i.e. below to about flat versus USD 149.15 over 24 months. Probability 40%: consistent with the Q3 guide and a company plan that doubles revenue over five years while the price already reflects that outcome.

bear_case.name: bear
bear_case.description: Model-estimate scenario. AI/memory capex pauses or HBM supply catches up with demand; revenue falls back to about USD 800-900M, non-GAAP gross margin 43-46% with under-absorbed Farmers Branch costs, opex 28-30% of revenue, EPS about USD 1.15-1.75, and the multiple compresses to 22-30x. Implies roughly USD 25-52 per share (0.2-0.4x). Probability 30%: the stock has 86% annualised volatility, SK hynix is about a quarter of revenue and revenue went flat in FY25 and fell 2.5% year on year in Q3 FY25, so the cycle has turned quickly before.

catalysts.description: Q3 FY26 results (quarter ending 26 Sep 2026): guided USD 270M +/- 10M revenue, 54.0% +/- 1.5% non-GAAP gross margin and USD 0.86 +/- 0.09 non-GAAP EPS; also the first read on DRAM growth after the +49% Q2 print and on Triton CPO shipments.
catalysts.window: about 28 Oct to 4 Nov 2026 (not announced as of 5 Oct 2026; inferred from 29 Oct 2025 and 29 Jul 2026 timing)

catalysts.description: Farmers Branch, Texas factory: production expected to begin late in Q4 FY26 with a ramp to initial target production levels over FY27, intended to add capacity and gross-margin accretion; start-up costs were USD 4.9M in Q2 FY26 and USD 11.9M in the first half.

Completion of the 2026 restructuring: Baldwin Park stopped manufacturing in January 2026 and the Carlsbad site is expected to manufacture through December 2026, with USD 30-40M of total charges guided and the stated aim of supporting gross-margin improvement.

Q4 FY26 results and FY27 first-quarter guide: whether revenue keeps climbing toward the company's USD 1.6B 2030 plan (current annualised guide about USD 1.08B) and whether gross margin holds above 50% as the new factory starts.
catalysts.window: Feb 2027 (date not confirmed; Q4 FY25 was reported 4 Feb 2026)

risks: Customer concentration: SK hynix was 24.3% of Q2 FY26 revenue (26.8% for the first half) and TSMC 11.0%; the top 10% customers together were 35.3% of Q2 revenue and three customers were 17.1%, 16.9% and 12.9% of gross receivables; Taiwan was 36.6% and South Korea 28.4% of Q2 revenue (e4).

Memory and AI capex cyclicality: DRAM was 32.9% of Q2 revenue and HBM growth explained about 75% of the year-on-year DRAM increase; revenue was nearly flat in FY25 (+2.8%) and fell 2.5% year on year in Q3 FY25, so demand has turned quickly before; the 10-K says there is generally not sufficient backlog to meet quarterly revenue and revenue depends on in-quarter orders (e3, e10).

Valuation and crowding: about 43x annualised guided non-GAAP EPS, about 69x trailing EPS, about 30x the company's own 2030 EPS target, 12-1 month momentum +149%, 37% above its 200-day average, 86% annualised volatility; very little margin for a guidance miss (e11, e12).

Target-model dependence: the 2030 plan relies on share gains in GPU, custom ASIC and CPO, which the company describes as mostly in qualification or initial ramp, with some nascent markets and limited visibility; achieving 36% share by 2030 (about 28% on the trailing figures) is a company aspiration, not a forecast (e8, e9).

Margin quality: gross margin rose sharply on mix and factory utilisation; GAAP gross margin was 38.4% in Q1 FY26 because of USD 21.5M of restructuring charges in cost of revenue; Farmers Branch start-up costs, new capacity and a possible pricing response could pressure the 54% guide; non-GAAP excludes restructuring and stock compensation (e3, e6, e7).

Execution: simultaneous factory consolidation (Carlsbad, Baldwin Park), a new Texas plant and ramps of HBM4 and CPO products; supplier concentration for substrates and boards with purchase orders rather than long-term contracts (e6, e7, e10).

Competition: the 10-K lists Japan Electronic Materials, Micronics Japan, Technoprobe, MPI, STAr, Korea Instrument and others in probe cards, several using similar MEMS technology; the Investor Day shows unnamed competitors in each segment; market-share data are company/Yole estimates only (e9, e10).

Cash flow volatility: FY25 free cash flow was only about USD 11.7M (operating cash flow USD 115.4M less capex USD 103.7M) in a period of heavy capex that included the Texas site purchase; free cash flow was USD 83.3M in the first half of FY26, so the improvement is recent (e1, e3).
Trade and geopolitical: export controls and US-China restrictions, tariffs (the company expects USD 7-9M of IEEPA tariff refunds in Q3 FY26) and a Taiwan/Korea-heavy customer base (e3, e4).

Not verified: no earnings-call transcript (Q1 or Q2 FY26) was read; call commentary on HBM4 share gains, DRAM shifting from HBM to DDR and CPO revenue above USD 20M in 2026 appears only in AI-generated secondary summaries and is not used as FACT (e13). Sell-side consensus and price history were not verified in this session.

Growth source is lumpier than the thesis implies: about 64% of the Q2 FY26 sequential revenue gain came from Systems (Triton CPO test: USD 27.9M to USD 48.5M; Q1 was down 20% year on year), DRAM rose only 2.5% sequentially and SK hynix revenue fell about 6% sequentially (e21, e22). The Q2 inflection is therefore not simply an HBM probe-card story.
Decelerating DRAM and SK hynix growth: DRAM year-on-year growth slowed from +69.7% to +49.0% and SK hynix from about +67% to about +28% (e22); the Q3 guide midpoint adds only 4.6% sequentially.

Customer set is broader and shifts quarter to quarter: NVIDIA was 10.2% of Q1 FY26 revenue, TSMC 11.0% of Q2, Intel 12.4% of Q2 FY25 and then below 10%; three customers were 46.9% of Q2 gross receivables (e4, e21, e23).

Memory-cycle extreme: Micron's quarterly revenue was USD 54.2B versus USD 11.3B a year earlier and its capex USD 10.8B a quarter (e25); both a demand signal and a sign that memory profit pools are at a cycle extreme, which has historically been followed by capex digestion in FORM's own history (FY22-FY23 revenue -14%, 2024-25 stock -62%) (e27, e28).

Competition: Technoprobe reported H1 2026 revenue +42.4% versus FORM +31.9% and raised its full-year guide; FORM's Foundry and Logic line grew about +26% in H1, so the plan to gain GPU/ASIC share is not yet visible in the numbers (e26).

Price path and volatility: the stock fell 43% in four weeks to 29 Jul 2026 (83.45) before a +26% one-day jump on the Q2 print and a further rise to 149.15, about 5.1x in 13 months; the mean analyst target of USD 145.44 is below the price (e24, e30).

Data quality: sell-side consensus, institutional ownership, short interest, a call transcript and the Q3 report date are not verified; the Investor Day TTM (USD 884M revenue, EPS USD 1.96) used the Q2 outlook and differs from the actual TTM (USD 902.2M, USD 2.17), already noted in e8/e11.

valuation.notes: Price USD 149.15 (2 Oct 2026); 78.12M shares outstanding (29 Jul 2026). TTM = Q3 FY25 to Q2 FY26 (USD 902.2M revenue; non-GAAP EPS 0.33+0.46+0.56+0.82). Annualised guide = Q3 FY26 midpoint x4. 2030 target EPS USD 5.00 is a company target, not guidance. Non-GAAP figures are company-defined.

exit_rules.condition: Non-GAAP gross margin below 50% in any quarter after the Texas factory starts (Q2 FY26 53.3%, Q3 guide 54.0% +/- 1.5%), or revenue falling sequentially by more than 10%, checkable in the quarterly earnings release.
Quarterly non-GAAP EPS below USD 0.70 (Q2 FY26 USD 0.82; Q3 guide USD 0.86 +/- 0.09), or two consecutive quarters of revenue at or below the low end of company guidance (USD 260M for Q3 FY26).
Farmers Branch has not begun production by the Q1 FY27 earnings release (about Feb to May 2027), or factory start-up costs remain above USD 5M a quarter after the stated start date.
Price above about USD 175 (about 50x annualised Q3 FY26 guided EPS) unless the annualised run-rate EPS from the latest guide or actuals has risen above about USD 3.5.

DRAM probe-card revenue growth below +20% year on year for two consecutive quarters (Q2 FY26 +49.0%), or SK hynix share of revenue falling below 15% while DRAM revenue is flat or down, both checkable in the 10-Q.

adversarial.strongest_bear_case: Peak-cycle numbers at a peak-cycle multiple: 43x guided EPS and 30x the company's own 2030 EPS target after a 5.1x move in 13 months, with SK hynix at about a quarter of revenue and Micron/SK hynix profits at an extreme. The Q2 inflection was two-thirds lumpy Systems (down 20% in Q1), DRAM grew 2.5% sequentially, SK hynix revenue fell about 6% sequentially, the Q3 guide adds only 4.6%, and Technoprobe is growing faster in AI logic. FORM fell 62% after its 2024 HBM run while revenue grew 2.8%; a memory capex pause gives EPS of USD 1.15-1.75 at 22-30x, i.e. USD 25-52.

questions.what_evidence_would_make_it_wrong: The cautious stance (strong company, price already capitalises the 2030 plan, no asymmetric entry) would be wrong on the low side if Q3 revenue exceeds about USD 285M with non-GAAP gross margin above 54% and Systems/CPO and HBM4 orders keep climbing: FORM beat the top of its guide in Q2 (e2), Micron's revenue is up 379% year on year (e25) and the company says it already reached its 2020 target model. Evidence that has already appeared against the thesis' demand story: about 64% of the Q2 sequential increase was Systems, DRAM grew 2.5% sequentially and SK hynix revenue fell about 6% (e22), Technoprobe is growing faster (e26). The cautious stance would be vindicated by a Systems revenue drop back toward USD 28M, SK hynix share falling and gross margin below 51%.
questions.what_is_missing: No call transcript (the third-party page could not be read and IR returned 503, so management remarks stay INFERENCE, e13); no consensus EPS/revenue or whether the Q3 guide is above or below it (only target prices, e30); no identification of the Triton/CPO customer or of how recurring Systems revenue is; no disclosure of HBM probe-card revenue, share versus Technoprobe/MJC/MPI, pricing, or order backlog (the 10-K says there is generally not enough backlog, e10); no ownership or short-interest data; the Q3 report date is an assumption (e31). The thesis also omitted NVIDIA at 10.2% of Q1 revenue and Intel's loss of 10% status (e21, e23), the sequential decomposition (e22) and the July drawdown (e24).
questions.is_catalyst_priced_in: Mostly priced. After the Q2 print the stock rose 26% in one day and is up about 41% since (105.38 to 149.15), and on 30 Sep it rose 9.6% on the day Micron reported (e24, e25), so the memory-super-cycle catalyst was digested within a session. Consensus estimates could not be checked, but the mean analyst target (USD 145.44) is below the price (e30) and the price already equals about 30x the company's own 2030 EPS target (e19). The next print needs to beat a guide that implies +4.6% sequential growth, and the company has beaten its guide before, so a beat is probably expected; I cannot size it.
questions.does_valuation_fit_growth: Not on durable growth. The multiple is 43x annualised guided EPS and 69x trailing (arithmetic verified), with year-on-year growth of about 32% but slowing sequentially (+14.2% to +4.6% guided) and with DRAM growth decelerating (e22). Revenue history is cyclical (FY21 770, FY23 663, FY25 785; e27) and the 10-K says there is generally no backlog (e10). To reach a 25x P/E on today's price EPS would have to be about USD 6.0 (1.7x the annualised guide), above the company's own 2030 target of USD 5.00, which is why the thesis' conclusion that the price already includes the plan checks out.
questions.great_company_vs_great_stock: Evidence suggests a much better company than a year ago (non-GAAP gross margin 38.5% to 53.3%, EPS 0.27 to 0.82, net cash about USD 334M) but the stock has already risen about 5.1x in 13 months and trades at about 12.5x TTM EV/sales, 30x the company's 2030 EPS target and above the mean analyst target (e24, e30). Great company, and at this price a stock whose payoff depends on the plan being exceeded while the cycle stays at an extreme.
questions.merely_an_ai_narrative: Not merely a narrative: revenue (+32% y/y), gross margin and EPS (tripled) are in the filings, HBM drove about 75% of the DRAM increase and Triton drove Systems (e3). But FY25 revenue was only +2.8% in a year when HBM was already hot (e1), the Q2 sequential gain was mostly Systems (e22), CPO revenue size comes only from unverified summaries (e13), and the valuation (43x guided EPS) exceeds what current revenue evidence supports, so narrative carries a large share of the multiple.
questions.is_it_crowded: The evidence suggests crowded: momentum rank 10 and +149% 12-1 month (e12), a 5.1x move in 13 months, 37% above the 200-day average, 86% annualised volatility, average daily value about USD 140M, and a price above the mean analyst target (e24, e30). Insider sales are modest (e29). The competitor Technoprobe also re-rated on the same theme (e26). Institutional ownership, short interest and flow data were not verified, so the degree of crowding cannot be quantified.
questions.strongest_bear_argument: As its best advocate would put it: FormFactor makes a cyclical consumable for memory and logic fabs and has just printed peak-cycle numbers. Micron's revenue is 4.8x year on year and SK hynix, 24-27% of FORM's revenue, is the very customer whose shipments are at a cycle extreme (e25). Strip the numbers: Q2's sequential growth was two-thirds Systems, a lumpy product that was down 20% in Q1, DRAM grew 2.5% sequentially and SK hynix revenue fell about 6% (e22); the Q3 guide adds only 4.6%; a faster-growing competitor (Technoprobe) is taking the AI logic business (e26); gross margin has gone from 38% to 54% in a year on mix and utilisation that can reverse as the Texas plant starts. At 43x guided EPS and 30x the 2030 target, with the stock already 5.1x in 13 months, the same stock fell 62% after its 2024 HBM run while revenue grew 2.8% (e28). A pause leaves EPS of USD 1.15-1.75 at 22-30x, USD 25-52.
questions.what_happened_in_similar_setups: Three analogues from sources I could open: (1) FORM in 2024: HBM/AI enthusiasm took the stock from about 39 to 61.7 (Jul 2024) and it then fell to 23.2 (Apr 2025), -62%, with FY25 revenue +2.8%; (2) FORM after the FY21 peak: revenue USD 770M to USD 663M (-14%) and the stock about 44-45 to about 19.7 (-56%); (3) VIAV after FY22: revenue -23% and the stock -59% (e27, e28, e33 in the VIAV thesis). These are same-company/sector anecdotes from a sampled price series; I did not find or read a base-rate study of multi-fold small caps. The present cycle is larger and supported by Micron and peers (e25), so history is a caution, not a forecast.
questions.what_must_happen_for_5x: A 5x outcome is USD 745.75, about USD 58.3B equity value. At the current 12.5x EV/TTM sales it needs about USD 4.6B annual revenue (5.1x TTM and above the company's own USD 4.5B 2030 served market); at 40x non-GAAP EPS it needs about USD 18.6 (8.6x TTM EPS, 3.7x the 2030 target) (e32). Operationally that means revenue and margin reaching more than three times the company's plan, with SAM, share and the multiple all far above plan, and no memory-cycle pause.
questions.is_5x_plausible_in_1_2_years: No. I estimate under 2% (model estimate); even a 3x needs EPS about 2x the 2030 target (author's e19/mechanism). A more realistic range is the author's: bull about 1.25-1.55x, base about 0.65-1.0x, bear about 0.2-0.4x. I would not lower the bull probability (30%) mechanically: annualised guided revenue is already USD 1.08B so the USD 1.4B bull revenue needs only about 3% sequential growth for eight quarters; the skew is instead in the multiple (43x guided EPS) and the memory-cycle risk, and a 43% fall in four weeks in July (e24) shows how quickly the bear range can be reached.
questions.probability_market_already_right: Model estimate: about 55-60% that the price is about right, i.e. that there is no edge at the 12-24 month horizon. Reasons: the stock rose 5.1x in 13 months and now exceeds the mean analyst target and about 30x the company's 2030 EPS (e30, e19); the author's scenario expected value is about 0.85x; but the company has repeatedly beaten its guides, Micron's numbers show a memory super-cycle and the plan appears conservative relative to the current USD 1.08B run-rate (e25), so the price is not obviously too high either. Consensus could not be checked.

evidence.claim: FormFactor revenue was USD 785.0M in FY25 (+2.8%), USD 763.6M in FY24 and USD 663.1M in FY23; FY25 net income USD 54.4M; operating cash flow USD 115.4M and capex USD 103.7M.

evidence.claim: Q2 FY26 revenue was USD 258.2M, up 14.2% sequentially and 31.9% year on year; non-GAAP gross margin 53.3% (GAAP 50.7%) versus 38.5% a year earlier; non-GAAP EPS USD 0.82 versus USD 0.27; free cash flow USD 52.6M; revenue, gross margin and EPS exceeded the high end of the outlook range. Q3 FY26 outlook: revenue USD 270M +/- 10M, non-GAAP gross margin 54.0% +/- 1.5%, non-GAAP EPS USD 0.86 +/- 0.09.
evidence.note: 8-K Exhibit 99.01 earnings release.

evidence.claim: Q2 FY26 revenue by market: Foundry and Logic USD 121.8M (+22.4%), DRAM USD 85.0M (+49.0%), Flash USD 2.9M (-48.4%), Systems USD 48.5M (+44.1%); HBM growth accounted for about 75% (Q2) and 69% (first half) of the year-on-year DRAM increase; the Systems increase was driven by Triton, the high-volume co-packaged-optics test system; first-half FY26 segment gross margin Probe Cards 52.5% and Systems 44.7%.
evidence.note: Form 10-Q MD&A.

evidence.claim: Customers at or above 10% of revenue in Q2 FY26: SK hynix 24.3% (26.8% in the first half) and TSMC 11.0%, together 35.3%; three customers were 17.1%, 16.9% and 12.9% of gross receivables; Taiwan was 36.6% and South Korea 28.4% of Q2 revenue; SK hynix was 19.2% to 25.0% of quarterly revenue across 2025 quarters.
evidence.note: 10-Q Note 2 and MD&A; 2025 quarterly history from the FY25 10-K. ANNOTATED by adversarial review: Q1 FY26 had SK hynix 29.5% and NVIDIA 10.2% (e21) and Q2 FY25 had Intel at 12.4%; the thesis listed only the Q2 FY26 names. See e21-e23.

evidence.claim: FormFactor acquired Keystone Photonics (silicon-photonics optical probing technology) on 15 Dec 2025 for USD 20.6M net of cash; the FY25 10-K says it is collaborating with customers to move co-packaged optics test from lab to fab and that SiPh and CPO moving to high-volume production may provide new growth.
evidence.note: Form 10-Q Note on acquisitions; 10-K business section for the CPO text.

evidence.claim: On 5 Jan 2026 FormFactor adopted restructuring plans to consolidate its Carlsbad and Baldwin Park manufacturing sites (200-300 employees affected), with about USD 30-40M of GAAP charges (about USD 20-25M non-cash, USD 10-15M cash) and actions largely complete by end of Dec 2026; Q1 FY26 cost of revenue included USD 21.5M of restructuring charges, which cut GAAP gross margin to 38.4% versus 49.0% non-GAAP.
evidence.note: 8-K Items 2.05/2.06; Q1 charge from the Q2 FY26 release non-GAAP reconciliation (e2 source).

evidence.claim: FormFactor bought a manufacturing site in Farmers Branch, Texas in June 2025 and expects to begin production late in Q4 FY26 with a ramp to initial target levels over FY27; factory start-up costs were USD 4.9M in Q2 FY26 and USD 11.9M in the first half; the company expects the facility to add capacity and a more favourable cost structure once ramped.
evidence.note: Form 10-Q MD&A Recent Developments.

evidence.claim: At its 11 May 2026 Investor Day FormFactor set a 2030 target model of USD 1.6B revenue (versus USD 884M TTM and USD 850M in the 2020 model), 55% non-GAAP gross margin, 23% opex, USD 5.00 non-GAAP EPS and about USD 510M operating income; it assumes a USD 4.5B served addressable market in 2030 (USD 4.0B probes, USD 0.5B systems) versus USD 3.1B TTM and a 36% market share by 2030; sustaining capex 4-5% of revenue; the company says the model is not guidance.

evidence.claim: The Investor Day states that growth drivers (ASICs, GPU, CPO and HBM) are mostly existing products in qualification or initial ramp, that some markets are nascent with limited visibility, and that market-share gains are targeted primarily in GPU, custom ASICs and CPO; it also shows unnamed competitors A-D in each probe segment.
